sanskrit: aṣṭau yasyāgnayo hy ete na dahante manaḥ sadā sa tad brahma śubhaṃ yāti yasmād bhūyo na vidyate
english: He in whom these eight fires never burn the mind—he attains that auspicious Brahman, beyond which nothing further is found.

sanskrit: ekādaśa ca yāny āhur indriyāṇi viśeṣataḥ ahaṃkāraprasūtāni tāni vakṣyāmy ahaṃ dvijāḥ
english: And the eleven that they call, in particular, the sense-organs—born of egoism—those I shall now expound, O twice-born ones.

sanskrit: śrotraṃ tvak cakṣuṣī jihvā nāsikā caiva pañcamī pādau pāyur upasthaṃ ca hastau vāg daśamī bhavet
english: The ear, the skin, the two eyes, the tongue, and the nose as the fifth; the two feet, the anus, and the organ of generation, the two hands, and speech as the tenth.

sanskrit: indriyagrāma ity eṣa mana ekādaśaṃ bhavet etaṃ grāmaṃ jayet pūrvaṃ tato brahma prakāśate
english: This is called the aggregate of the senses, with the mind as the eleventh. Let one first conquer this aggregate; thereupon Brahman shines forth.

sanskrit: buddhīndriyāṇi pañcāhuḥ pañca karmendriyāṇi ca śrotrādīny api pañcāhur buddhiyuktāni tattvataḥ
english: Five they call the organs of knowledge, and five the organs of action; the ear and the rest, five in number, they declare to be in truth conjoined with intellect.

sanskrit: aviśeṣāṇi cānyāni karmayuktāni tāni tu ubhayatra mano jñeyaṃ buddhir dvādaśamī bhavet
english: And the others, undistinguished, are those conjoined with action; in both groups the mind is to be known as present, and intellect would be the twelfth.

sanskrit: ity uktānīndriyāṇīmāny ekādaśa mayā kramāt manyante kṛtam ity eva viditvaitāni paṇḍitāḥ
english: Thus have these eleven senses been declared by me in order; knowing these, the wise consider their task accomplished.

sanskrit: trīṇi sthānāni bhūtānāṃ caturthaṃ nopapadyate sthalam āpas tathākāśaṃ janma cāpi caturvidham
english: Three are the abodes of beings; a fourth does not arise—dry land, the waters, and the sky; and birth, too, is of four kinds.

sanskrit: aṇḍajodbhijjasaṃsvedajarāyujam athāpi ca caturdhā janma ity etad bhūtagrāmasya lakṣyate
english: Egg-born, sprout-born, sweat-born, and womb-born—thus the birth of the aggregate of beings is observed to be of four kinds.

sanskrit: acarāṇy api bhūtāni khecarāṇi tathaiva ca aṇḍajāni vijānīyāt sarvāṃś caiva sarīsṛpān
english: Even the immobile beings, and likewise those that move in the sky, one should know to be egg-born, and so too all the creeping things.

sanskrit: saṃsvedāḥ kṛmayaḥ proktā jantavaś ca tathāvidhāḥ janma dvitīyam ity etaj jaghanyataram ucyate
english: Worms and creatures of like kind are declared to be sweat-born; this second mode of birth is said to be the lowliest.

sanskrit: bhittvā tu pṛthivīṃ yāni jāyante kālaparyayāt udbhijjānīti tāny āhur bhūtāni dvijasattamāḥ
english: Those beings which, bursting through the earth, are born as time rolls on—these they call sprout-born, O most excellent of the twice-born.

sanskrit: dvipādabahupādāni tiryaggatimatīni ca jarāyujāni bhūtāni vitta tāny api sattamāḥ
english: Beings two-footed and many-footed, and those that move on a slanting course—know these too to be womb-born, O most excellent ones.

sanskrit: dvividhāpīha vijñeyā brahmayoniḥ sanātanā tapaḥ karma ca yat puṇyam ity eṣa viduṣāṃ nayaḥ
english: The eternal source that is Brahman is here to be known as twofold: austerity, and meritorious action—such is the doctrine of the wise.

sanskrit: dvividhaṃ karma vijñeyam ijyā dānaṃ ca yan makhe jātasyādhyayanaṃ puṇyam iti vṛddhānuśāsanam
english: Action is to be known as twofold: sacrifice, and the giving of gifts at the rite. The study of one who has been born is meritorious—such is the teaching of the elders.

sanskrit: etad yo veda vidhivat sa muktaḥ syād dvijarṣabhāḥ vimuktaḥ sarvapāpebhya iti caiva nibodhata
english: He who knows this duly would be liberated, O bulls among the twice-born; and know him, too, to be freed from all sins.

sanskrit: ākāśaṃ prathamaṃ bhūtaṃ śrotram adhyātmam ucyate adhibhūtaṃ tathā śabdo diśas tatrādhidaivatam
english: Ether is the first element; the ear is called its relation to the self; sound is its relation to beings; and the quarters of space are therein the presiding divinity.

sanskrit: dvitīyaṃ māruto bhūtaṃ tvag adhyātmaṃ ca viśrutam spraṣṭavyam adhibhūtaṃ ca vidyut tatrādhidaivatam
english: The second element is wind; the skin is renowned as its relation to the self; the tangible is its relation to beings; and lightning is therein the presiding divinity.

sanskrit: tṛtīyaṃ jyotir ity āhuś cakṣur adhyātmam ucyate adhibhūtaṃ tato rūpaṃ sūryas tatrādhidaivatam
english: The third they call light; the eye is said to be its relation to the self; form is then its relation to beings; and the sun is therein the presiding divinity.

sanskrit: caturtham āpo vijñeyaṃ jihvā cādhyātmam iṣyate adhibhūtaṃ rasaś cātra somas tatrādhidaivatam
english: The fourth is to be known as the waters; the tongue is held to be its relation to the self; taste is here its relation to beings; and Soma is therein the presiding divinity.

sanskrit: pṛthivī pañcamaṃ bhūtaṃ ghrāṇaś cādhyātmam iṣyate adhibhūtaṃ tathā gandho vāyus tatrādhidaivatam
english: Earth is the fifth element; the nose is held to be its relation to the self; smell is likewise its relation to beings; and Vāyu is therein the presiding divinity.

sanskrit: eṣa pañcasu bhūteṣu catuṣṭayavidhiḥ smṛtaḥ ataḥ paraṃ pravakṣyāmi sarvaṃ trividham indriyam
english: This fourfold ordering with respect to the five elements has been recounted; hereafter I shall expound the whole threefold reckoning of each sense-organ.

sanskrit: pādāv adhyātmam ity āhur brāhmaṇās tattvadarśinaḥ adhibhūtaṃ tu gantavyaṃ viṣṇus tatrādhidaivatam
english: The two feet, the brāhmaṇas who perceive the truth declare to be the relation to the self; that which is to be traversed is the relation to beings; and Viṣṇu is therein the presiding divinity.

sanskrit: avāggatir apānaś ca pāyur adhyātmam iṣyate adhibhūtaṃ visargaś ca mitras tatrādhidaivatam
english: The downward-moving breath, the apāna whose course is downward—the anus is held to be the relation to the self; excretion is the relation to beings; and Mitra is therein the presiding divinity.

sanskrit: prajanaḥ sarvabhūtānām upastho 'dhyātmam ucyate adhibhūtaṃ tathā śukraṃ daivataṃ ca prajāpatiḥ
english: The procreation of all beings—the organ of generation is called the relation to the self; semen, likewise, is the relation to beings; and the divinity is Prajāpati.

sanskrit: hastāv adhyātmam ity āhur adhyātmaviduṣo janāḥ adhibhūtaṃ tu karmāṇi śakras tatrādhidaivatam
english: The two hands, those who know the relation to the self declare to be the relation to the self; acts are the relation to beings; and Śakra is therein the presiding divinity.

sanskrit: vaiśvadevī manaḥpūrvā vāg adhyātmam ihocyate vaktavyam adhibhūtaṃ ca vahnis tatrādhidaivatam
english: Speech, sacred to all the gods and preceded by the mind, is here called the relation to the self; what is to be spoken is the relation to beings; and Agni is therein the presiding divinity.

sanskrit: adhyātmaṃ mana ity āhuḥ pañcabhūtānucārakam adhibhūtaṃ ca mantavyaṃ candramāś cādhidaivatam
english: The mind, follower of the five elements, they call the relation to the self; what is to be thought is the relation to beings; and the moon is the presiding divinity.

sanskrit: adhyātmaṃ buddhir ity āhuḥ ṣaḍindriyavicāriṇī adhibhūtaṃ tu vijñeyaṃ brahmā tatrādhidaivatam
english: The intellect, which ranges over the six senses, they call the relation to the self; what is to be discerned is the relation to beings; and Brahmā is therein the presiding divinity.

sanskrit: yathāvad adhyātmavidhir eṣa vaḥ kīrtito mayā jñānam asya hi dharmajñāḥ prāptaṃ buddhimatām iha
english: This ordering of the relation to the self has been duly proclaimed to you by me; for the knowledge of it, O knowers of dharma, is attained here by the wise.

sanskrit: indriyāṇīndriyārthāś ca mahābhūtāni pañca ca sarvāṇy etāni saṃdhāya manasā saṃpradhārayet
english: The senses, the objects of the senses, and the five great elements—gathering all these together with the mind, one should hold them firmly in contemplation.

sanskrit: kṣīṇe manasi sarvasmin na janmasukham iṣyate jñānasaṃpannasattvānāṃ tat sukhaṃ viduṣāṃ matam
english: When the entire mind has been dissolved, no happiness rooted in birth is sought; that happiness, in the view of the wise, belongs to those whose being is full of knowledge.

sanskrit: ataḥ paraṃ pravakṣyāmi sūkṣmabhāvakarīṃ śivām nivṛttiṃ sarvabhūteṣu mṛdunā dāruṇena vā
english: Hereafter I shall expound that auspicious cessation toward all beings—producing a subtle state—whether by gentle means or by harsh.

sanskrit: guṇāguṇam anāsaṅgam ekacaryam anantaram etad brāhmaṇato vṛttam āhur ekapadaṃ sukham
english: Free of the qualities yet endowed with quality, free of attachment, solitary in conduct, uninterrupted—this they call the conduct befitting the brāhmaṇa, the one abode of happiness.

sanskrit: vidvān kūrma ivāṅgāni kāmān saṃhṛtya sarvaśaḥ virajāḥ sarvato mukto yo naraḥ sa sukhī sadā
english: The wise man who, like a tortoise drawing in its limbs, withdraws all desires entirely—stainless and freed on every side—that man is forever happy.

sanskrit: kāmān ātmani saṃyamya kṣīṇatṛṣṇaḥ samāhitaḥ sarvabhūtasuhṛn maitro brahmabhūyaṃ sa gacchati
english: Restraining his desires within the self, with thirst extinguished and mind composed, a friend to all beings, full of goodwill, he goes to union with Brahman.

sanskrit: indriyāṇāṃ nirodhena sarveṣāṃ viṣayaiṣiṇām muner janapadatyāgād adhyātmāgniḥ samidhyate
english: By the restraint of all the senses that crave their objects, and by the sage's abandonment of inhabited regions, the fire of the inner self is kindled.

sanskrit: yathāgnir indhanair iddho mahājyotiḥ prakāśate tathendriyanirodhena mahān ātmā prakāśate
english: As fire kindled by fuel shines forth as a great light, so by the restraint of the senses the great Self shines forth.

sanskrit: yadā paśyati bhūtāni prasannātmātmano hṛdi svayaṃyonis tadā sūkṣmāt sūkṣmam āpnoty anuttamam
english: When, with serene self, one beholds all beings within the heart of the self, then, self-originated, one attains the unsurpassed, subtler than the subtle.

sanskrit: agnī rūpaṃ payaḥ sroto vāyuḥ sparśanam eva ca mahī paṅkadharaṃ ghoram ākāśaṃ śravaṇaṃ tathā
english: Fire is form, water is the flowing stream, and wind is touch; earth is the dreadful bearer of mire, and ether is hearing.

sanskrit: rāgaśokasamāviṣṭaṃ pañcasrotaḥsamāvṛtam pañcabhūtasamāyuktaṃ navadvāraṃ dvidaivatam
english: Pervaded by passion and grief, encompassed by five streams, conjoined with the five elements, having nine gates and two presiding deities—

sanskrit: rajasvalam athādṛśyaṃ triguṇaṃ ca tridhātukam saṃsargābhirataṃ mūḍhaṃ śarīram iti dhāraṇā
english: full of rajas, yet unseen, possessed of the three qualities and the three humours, delighting in contact, deluded—such is the conception of the body.

sanskrit: duścaraṃ jīvaloke 'smin sattvaṃ prati samāśritam etad eva hi loke 'smin kālacakraṃ pravartate
english: Hard to traverse in this world of the living, it rests upon each individual existence; and it is this very thing that turns as the wheel of time in this world.

sanskrit: etan mahārṇavaṃ ghoram agādhaṃ mohasaṃjñitam visṛjet saṃkṣipec caiva bodhayet sāmaraṃ jagat
english: This dreadful, fathomless great ocean named delusion—one may let it loose or draw it in, and rouse to wakefulness the world together with its gods.

sanskrit: kāmakrodhau bhayaṃ moham abhidroham athānṛtam indriyāṇāṃ nirodhena sa tāṃs tyajati dustyajān
english: Desire and anger, fear, delusion, hostility, and falsehood—by the restraint of the senses he forsakes these things so hard to forsake.

sanskrit: yasyaite nirjitā loke triguṇāḥ pañca dhātavaḥ vyomni tasya paraṃ sthānam anantam atha lakṣyate
english: He by whom these five constituents bearing the three qualities are conquered in the world—for him the supreme, infinite abode is discerned in the firmament.

sanskrit: kāmakūlām apārāntāṃ manaḥsrotobhayāvahām nadīṃ durgahradāṃ tīrṇaḥ kāmakrodhāv ubhau jayet
english: Having crossed the river whose banks are desire, whose far shore is endless, fearful with the current of the mind, and dangerous with its whirlpools, one should conquer both desire and anger.

sanskrit: sa sarvadoṣanirmuktas tataḥ paśyati yat param mano manasi saṃdhāya paśyaty ātmānam ātmani
english: Freed from all faults, he then beholds what is supreme; fixing the mind within the mind, he beholds the Self within the self.

sanskrit: sarvavit sarvabhūteṣu vīkṣaty ātmānam ātmani ekadhā bahudhā caiva vikurvāṇas tatas tataḥ
english: All-knowing, in all beings he sees the Self within the self—now as one, now as many—transforming himself this way and that.

sanskrit: dhruvaṃ paśyati rūpāṇi dīpād dīpaśataṃ yathā sa vai viṣṇuś ca mitraś ca varuṇo 'gniḥ prajāpatiḥ
english: He surely beholds forms, as a hundred lamps are lit from a single lamp; he indeed is Viṣṇu and Mitra, Varuṇa, Agni, and Prajāpati.

sanskrit: sa hi dhātā vidhātā ca sa prabhuḥ sarvatomukhaḥ hṛdayaṃ sarvabhūtānāṃ mahān ātmā prakāśate
english: For he is the Ordainer and the Disposer; he is the Lord, facing in all directions; as the heart of all beings the great Self shines forth.

sanskrit: taṃ viprasaṃghāś ca surāsurāś ca; yakṣāḥ piśācāḥ pitaro vayāṃsi rakṣogaṇā bhūtagaṇāś ca sarve; maharṣayaś caiva sadā stuvanti
english: Him the assemblies of brāhmaṇas, and gods and demons, the yakṣas, the piśācas, the ancestors, the birds, the hosts of rākṣasas, and all the throngs of spirits, and the great seers as well, forever praise.

sanskrit: brahmovāca manuṣyāṇāṃ tu rājanyaḥ kṣatriyo madhyamo guṇaḥ kuñjaro vāhanānāṃ ca siṃhaś cāraṇyavāsinām
english: Brahmā said: Among men the foremost is the prince, the kṣatriya, of the middle quality; among beasts of burden, the elephant; and among forest-dwellers, the lion.

sanskrit: aviḥ paśūnāṃ sarveṣām ākhuś ca bilavāsinām gavāṃ govṛṣabhaś caiva strīṇāṃ puruṣa eva ca
english: The ram, among all the small cattle; and the rat, among dwellers in burrows; the bull, among cattle; and among women, the man indeed.

sanskrit: nyagrodho jambuvṛkṣaś ca pippalaḥ śālmalis tathā śiṃśapā meṣaśṛṅgaś ca tathā kīcakaveṇavaḥ ete drumāṇāṃ rājāno loke 'smin nātra saṃśayaḥ
english: The banyan and the jambu tree, the pippala and the śālmali, the śiṃśapā and the meṣaśṛṅga, and likewise the hollow, whistling bamboos—these are the kings among trees in this world; herein is no doubt.

sanskrit: himavān pāriyātraś ca sahyo vindhyas trikūṭavān śveto nīlaś ca bhāsaś ca kāṣṭhavāṃś caiva parvataḥ
english: Himavān and Pāriyātra, the Sahya, the Vindhya, the Trikūṭa, the Śveta and the Nīla, the Bhāsa, and the mountain rich in timber—

sanskrit: śubhaskandho mahendraś ca mālyavān parvatas tathā ete parvatarājāno gaṇānāṃ marutas tathā
english: the fair-shouldered, and Mahendra, and the mountain Mālyavān—these are the kings among mountains; and among hosts, likewise, the Maruts.

sanskrit: sūryo grahāṇām adhipo nakṣatrāṇāṃ ca candramāḥ yamaḥ pitṝṇām adhipaḥ saritām atha sāgaraḥ
english: The sun is lord of the planets, and the moon of the constellations; Yama is lord of the ancestors, and the ocean of the rivers.

sanskrit: ambhasāṃ varuṇo rājā sattvānāṃ mitra ucyate arko 'dhipatir uṣṇānāṃ jyotiṣām indur ucyate
english: Varuṇa is the king of the waters; Mitra is said to be the king of living creatures; the sun is the overlord of hot things, and the moon is called the king of the lights of heaven.

sanskrit: agnir bhūtapatir nityaṃ brāhmaṇānāṃ bṛhaspatiḥ oṣadhīnāṃ patiḥ somo viṣṇur balavatāṃ varaḥ
english: Agni is ever the lord of beings; Bṛhaspati is lord of the brāhmaṇas; Soma is lord of the healing herbs; and Viṣṇu is the foremost of the mighty.

sanskrit: tvaṣṭādhirājo rūpāṇāṃ paśūnām īśvaraḥ śivaḥ dakṣiṇānāṃ tathā yajño vedānām ṛṣayas tathā
english: Tvaṣṭṛ is the sovereign of forms; Śiva is the lord of beasts; the sacrifice, likewise, is lord of priestly fees; and the seers, of the Vedas.

sanskrit: diśām udīcī viprāṇāṃ somo rājā pratāpavān kuberaḥ sarvayakṣāṇāṃ devatānāṃ puraṃdaraḥ eṣa bhūtādikaḥ sargaḥ prajānāṃ ca prajāpatiḥ
english: Of the quarters, the north; of the brāhmaṇas, the glorious king Soma; Kubera, of all the yakṣas; and Purandara, of the gods. This is the creation beginning with the elements, and Prajāpati is the lord of creatures.

sanskrit: sarveṣām eva bhūtānām ahaṃ brahmamayo mahān bhūtaṃ parataraṃ matto viṣṇor vāpi na vidyate
english: Of all beings I am the great one, made of Brahman; no being higher than I, or than Viṣṇu, is found.

sanskrit: rājādhirājaḥ sarvāsāṃ viṣṇur brahmamayo mahān īśvaraṃ taṃ vijānīmaḥ sa vibhuḥ sa prajāpatiḥ
english: The king of all kings is Viṣṇu, the great one, made of Brahman; him we know to be the Lord—he is the all-pervading, he is Prajāpati.

sanskrit: narakiṃnarayakṣāṇāṃ gandharvoragarakṣasām devadānavanāgānāṃ sarveṣām īśvaro hi saḥ
english: For he is the Lord of all—of men, kiṃnaras, and yakṣas, of gandharvas, serpents, and rākṣasas, of gods, dānavas, and nāgas.

sanskrit: bhagadevānuyātānāṃ sarvāsāṃ vāmalocanā māheśvarī mahādevī procyate pārvatīti yā
english: Of all those fair-eyed ones who follow the god Bhaga, the great goddess, consort of Maheśvara, who is called Pārvatī, is proclaimed the highest.

sanskrit: umāṃ devīṃ vijānīta nārīṇām uttamāṃ śubhām ratīnāṃ vasumatyas tu strīṇām apsarasas tathā
english: Know the goddess Umā to be the most excellent and auspicious of women; among delights, the bounteous earths; and among women, likewise, the apsarases.

sanskrit: dharmakāmāś ca rājāno brāhmaṇā dharmalakṣaṇāḥ tasmād rājā dvijātīnāṃ prayateteha rakṣaṇe
english: Kings desire dharma, and brāhmaṇas bear the mark of dharma; therefore let the king strive here in the protection of the twice-born.

sanskrit: rājñāṃ hi viṣaye yeṣām avasīdanti sādhavaḥ hīnās te svaguṇaiḥ sarvaiḥ pretyāvāṅmārgagāminaḥ
english: For those kings in whose realm the virtuous sink into ruin—they, bereft of all their own merits, travel after death by the downward path.

sanskrit: rājñāṃ tu viṣaye yeṣāṃ sādhavaḥ parirakṣitāḥ te 'smiṃl loke pramodante pretya cānantyam eva ca prāpnuvanti mahātmāna iti vitta dvijarṣabhāḥ
english: But those kings in whose realm the virtuous are well protected—they rejoice in this world, and after death those great-souled ones attain the very state of infinity; know this, O bulls among the twice-born.

sanskrit: ata ūrdhvaṃ pravakṣyāmi niyataṃ dharmalakṣaṇam ahiṃsālakṣaṇo dharmo hiṃsā cādharmalakṣaṇā
english: Hereafter I shall expound the fixed defining mark of dharma: dharma has non-injury as its mark, and injury is the mark of unrighteousness.

sanskrit: prakāśalakṣaṇā devā manuṣyāḥ karmalakṣaṇāḥ śabdalakṣaṇam ākāśaṃ vāyus tu sparśalakṣaṇaḥ
english: The gods have radiance as their mark; men have action as their mark; ether has sound as its mark; and wind has touch as its mark.

sanskrit: jyotiṣāṃ lakṣaṇaṃ rūpam āpaś ca rasalakṣaṇāḥ dharaṇī sarvabhūtānāṃ pṛthivī gandhalakṣaṇā
english: The mark of the luminaries is form, and the waters have taste as their mark; the earth, bearer of all beings, has smell as her mark.

sanskrit: svaravyañjanasaṃskārā bhāratī satyalakṣaṇā manaso lakṣaṇaṃ cintā tathoktā buddhir anvayāt
english: Speech, refined with vowels and consonants, has truth as its mark; the mark of the mind is thought; and the intellect, accordingly, is so described by inference.

sanskrit: manasā cintayāno 'rthān buddhyā caiva vyavasyati buddhir hi vyavasāyena lakṣyate nātra saṃśayaḥ
english: Contemplating objects with the mind, one resolves upon them with the intellect; for the intellect is marked by determination—herein is no doubt.

sanskrit: lakṣaṇaṃ mahato dhyānam avyaktaṃ sādhulakṣaṇam pravṛttilakṣaṇo yogo jñānaṃ saṃnyāsalakṣaṇam
english: Meditation is the mark of the Great Principle; the unmanifest has the mark of the holy; yoga has the mark of activity, and knowledge has the mark of renunciation.

sanskrit: tasmāj jñānaṃ puraskṛtya saṃnyased iha buddhimān saṃnyāsī jñānasaṃyuktaḥ prāpnoti paramāṃ gatim atīto 'dvaṃdvam abhyeti tamomṛtyujarātigam
english: Therefore, placing knowledge foremost, let the wise man here renounce; the renunciant, joined with knowledge, attains the supreme goal—transcending the pairs of opposites, he approaches that which is beyond darkness, death, and old age.

sanskrit: dharmalakṣaṇasaṃyuktam uktaṃ vo vidhivan mayā guṇānāṃ grahaṇaṃ samyag vakṣyāmy aham ataḥ param
english: That which is joined with the defining marks of dharma has been duly declared to you by me; hereafter I shall rightly expound the apprehension of the qualities.

sanskrit: pārthivo yas tu gandho vai ghrāṇeneha sa gṛhyate ghrāṇasthaś ca tathā vāyur gandhajñāne vidhīyate
english: The smell that belongs to earth is here grasped by the nose; and the wind seated in the nose is appointed to the knowledge of smell.

sanskrit: apāṃ dhāturaso nityaṃ jihvayā sa tu gṛhyate jihvāsthaś ca tathā somo rasajñāne vidhīyate
english: The essence that is the constituent of the waters is ever grasped by the tongue; and Soma, seated in the tongue, is appointed to the knowledge of taste.
